title: Moon Spirit
description: A Kachina-like figure rising from a blood moon. Dense hatching meets flat red.
process: Started with the red circle, painted flat and left to dry. Everything else was built in fine liner on top — the figure emerged slowly, tile by tile.
inspiration: Hopi Kachina dolls. The idea that a spirit can have a body that is simultaneously geometric and alive.
meaning: Something about ritual and stillness. The figure isn't doing anything — just being present against the red.

title: Trip Shi — I
description: Tiled, mirrored, obsessive. A body fractured into geometric pattern.
process: Drew on individual Post-it notes, then arranged and rearranged them until the symmetry felt right. No digital tools.
inspiration: Islamic geometric tilework, and the way repeating units can build a face.
meaning: The self as pattern. Identity as something assembled, not given.
